text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz accused the Gdansk shipyard trade unionists of aggression and law breaking in a parliamentary speech yesterday.

- Young activists of the right-leaning Confederation for an Independent Poland (KPN) urged Cimoszewicz to dismiss Construction Minister Barbara Blida, whom they blamed for advancing deterioration of the housing industry. Blida said the housing sector was improving year by year.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Szczecin shipyard and Polska Zegluga Morska (PZM) shipping firm may form a joint venture to take over part of the Gdansk shipyard's assets and employ 2,000 workers of the bankrupt yard, Cimoszewicz said.

- Autostrada Wielkopolska motorway construction consortium will complete a 360 km stretch of the A-2 motorway from Swiecko on the Polish-German border to Strykow, central Poland, in up to 10 years time, the consortium said. Autostrada Wielkopolska will tender for contracts for other stretches of the A-2.

- Poland's 1997 passenger car duty free import quota was 38,750 cars, the economy ministry said. The biggest individual importers were Fiat Auto Poland, which imported 4,642 cars, Kulczyk Tradex - 3,256 Volkswagen, Audi and Porsche cars, Iberia Motor - 3,200 Seats and Citroen Poland - 2,837 Citroens.

- Poland's steel industry delegation to Brussels is now negotiating an extension of the industry's protection period with the European Commission as well as EU restructuring subsidies for the sector. The Polish steel industry's restructuring will cost up to $4.5 billion.
- Trade unions at the Fasta cotton textile plant in Bialystok have accepted 650 redundancies by the year end. The plant will then employ 2,050 workers, the management said.

- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank has opened a branch office in Moscow. BGZ is planning to form a joint venture with a Russian bank and is seeking a partner, BGZ president Kazimierz Oleksiak said.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy has applied for an operating licence to start a bank providing services to expatriate residents in Moscow, the bank said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Barclays de Zoete Wedd will act as consultant in the planned B-series share issue by Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU), Poland biggest insurance firm, PZU's spokesperson Marek Maszek said.
PARKIET - Lubawa technical clothing maker has raised its 1997 net profit forecast to 2.7 million zlotys, the management said.

- Compensa SA insurance firm will list its shares on the Warsaw bourse this year along with its Warta and Polisa competitors. Compensa has decided on a share listing as it will prove the company's transparency and provide monitoring of its operations, Compensa's president Krzysztof Lutostanski said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
